parsed.summary: The first theorem proves that there is a connected, bipartite, 2-degenerate finite graph H with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all large n, for some c, ε > 0. It also adds the condition that in every proper 2-colouring, each colour class contains a vertex of degree > 2. The second theorem proves the negation of Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate graph (r > 0) satisfies ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}). The definitions appear faithful; the only deviation is the extra degree conjunct, which makes the Lean statement stronger than the paper.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s, the neighbours of v inside the finite set s
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood restricted to a vertex subset

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex with at most r neighbours in s (the induced subgraph on s has minimum degree ≤ r).
glossary.note: Using induced subgraphs is equivalent to the paper's 'every nonempty subgraph' formulation, since deleting edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every finite bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q: ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞.
glossary.note: The hypothesis r > 0 excludes 1/0; the r = 0 case is trivial anyway.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q, together with reals c > 0 and ε > 0, such that: H is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate; for every proper 2-colouring of H, each colour class contains a vertex of degree > 2; and for all sufficiently large n, c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) (Mathlib extremalNumber).
There exist r > 0 and a finite bipartite r-degenerate graph H such that ex(n,H) is not O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 such that ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Not every bipartite r-degenerate graph satisfies ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}); this fails already for r = 2.
Failure of compactness (covered elsewhere, sibling file).

coverage.why: Matches the paper's statement, plus an extra conjunct that both colour classes have maximum degree > 2.
This is the negation of a faithful formalisation of conjecture (3).

flags.explanation: Extra conjunct not in Theorem 1.2: under every proper 2-colouring, each side has a vertex of degree > 2. This rules out the known Füredi/AKS case. It only strengthens the statement. It also forces both colour classes to be nonempty, since the sup over an empty side is 0.

lint_verdicts.why: This is the Finset.card of a finite filter, so it has no junk value.
The hypothesis 0 < r excludes 1/0, and the exponent is a genuine real 2 − 1/r.
